notice.title: Notice to our guests — 14 July 2026
notice.body: Following the instructions of the archipelago authorities, and as a precaution due to instability at the glacier front, the Arca remains temporarily closed. All scheduled stays have been cancelled and will be refunded in full. Reopening expected within the next 72 hours.

home.title:
Where time
stands still
home.subtitle: Thirty-two suites between glacier and sea. Svalbard, Norway.
home.intro: One hundred and twenty kilometres from Longyearbyen, the Arca overlooks an inlet with no roads or villages in sight. Timber and stone suites, Nordic cuisine and a glass lounge facing the glacier. The final stretch is by helicopter or by sea. From there, we take care of everything.
zeros: Heat pumps, electric mobility and water treatment. Our idea of luxury begins with caring for the place that welcomes us.
An acoustic joint separates the Aurora from the building. The machinery keeps working. The glasses remain still.
A late breakfast, a paddle beneath the midnight sun, an unhurried evening at the table. There is time to stay.
home.quote: In the Aurora, the landscape does not stay beyond the window: it fills the room. A hotel worth the journey to the end of the coast.
home.suiteText: From the glazed garden to the Crown Suite, at the very top of the building.
home.experiencesTitle:
A stay
at your own pace.
home.auroraText: Ten metres of curved glass, a mahogany table for twelve and the glacier on your left.
home.wellnessText: The warmth of the water. The stillness of the glacier.
home.expeditionsText: The glacier on foot and the inlet by kayak. In winter, a sky lit by the northern lights. Always with our guides.
home.bookingNote: The hotel remains closed. All scheduled stays have been cancelled and will be refunded in full.

arca.title:
Architecture
for the Arctic.
arca.intro: Dark concrete on the slope, pale timber inside and windows open to the inlet. The Arca is built to inhabit this landscape in comfort, even in the depths of winter.
sections: Stone and timber

The building steps down the slope so that every suite has the inlet in front and no one above. The laminated timber comes from the forests of Trøndelag. The concrete was tinted on site to match the rock of the shore.
A joint for the glasses

The Aurora does not touch the rest of the building. It rests on the edge of the block, half of it cantilevered over the slope, separated by a hand-wide joint filled with rubber. During testing in the spring, the waiters left full glasses on the table while the generators started. Not one moved.
Keeping the cold out
Triple glazing, rock wool and heat pumps that draw warmth from the air even in winter. Outside it may be thirty below; in your suite it will be twenty-two.
arca.planTitle: From the dock to the spire.
levels: Main level · Aurora, restaurant, gallery and garden
arca.crown: On the roof of the rear wing stands a steel spire with a red light at its tip. We call it the Crown. It is the first thing you see from the air, and a landmark for pilots flying the coast at night.
arca.crownNote: In summer you hardly notice it. In the polar night it is the only thing you can see.

aurora.title:
A lounge open
to the horizon.
aurora.intro: Ten metres of curved glass, the inlet straight ahead and the glacier to the left. The Aurora is where you return after an outing and where you stay when you feel like going nowhere at all.
aurora.table: A single piece of mahogany, worked by a cabinetmaker in Bergen. Twelve chairs around the captain’s table. Every Saturday at nine, we serve a shared dinner here, leaving time for a long evening.
aurora.bar: Cocktails made to be drunk slowly while looking at the glacier. Also alcohol-free.
aurora.camNote: What is happening in the Aurora right now.

suites.title:
Your place
overlooking the inlet.
suites.intro: Three suite categories, the same care for your rest. Linen, stone and pale timber. Open views and room to settle in.

items.name: Garden Suites
items.body: They open onto the garden gallery, a glazed corridor with four rowan trees brought from Tromsø and “The Hand”, a bronze by Einar Velde. Beyond it, the inlet.

items.name: Upper Suites
items.body: In the upper wing of the building, with three-metre windows over the water. From the bed you can see the glacier front.
features: Bathtub, rain shower and underfloor heating
Binoculars and a small Arctic library

items.name: Crown Suite
items.body: The highest suite in the Arca, right beneath the Crown. It has its own dining room and a pantry stocked with whatever you ask for before you arrive.

suites.gardenText: The rowans in the gallery are in leaf in July and in January. It is the only thing in the Arca that does not follow the seasons.

dining.title:
The north,
at the table.
dining.intro: Cold-water fish, lamb and seasonal berries. Cooking led by its ingredients, with a short menu that follows the rhythm of our deliveries.
sections: The restaurant
Lunch and dinner on the main floor, overlooking the dock. If there is anything you cannot or do not eat, tell us when you book and you will not have to say it twice.
The cellar
Great Bordeaux vintages, champagne from small growers and a collection of Japanese whiskies that grows every season.
Saturdays in the Aurora
A tasting menu at the mahogany table, twelve guests, at nine. Book ahead, and finish without looking at the clock.
dining.menuNote: The menu changes with what arrives each week.

wellness.title:
A refuge
facing the ice.
wellness.intro: Sauna, treatments and an outdoor hot tub facing the glacier, at thirty-eight degrees.
wellness.spa: Open from seven in the morning until midnight, which in summer means during the day. Massages and treatments by appointment.
wellness.med: The Arca has its own medical service and an Omni-Med v4 diagnostic capsule. Connected in real time to our specialists in Zurich, it provides an initial assessment without leaving the hotel.
wellness.medNote: Medical service led by Dr Anya Tamm.

expeditions.title:
Outside,
the Arctic.
expeditions.intro: Our guides accompany you beyond the hotel. Routes chosen for the weather and terrain, small groups and all equipment prepared before you set out.
items: A walk up to the moraine with a guide who knows the ice. Never beneath the front: nobody goes near it.
The inlet at eleven at night, the water still and the sun still high. Groups of six, drysuits.
From October to March, night outings to watch the sky. Sometimes they do not appear. When they do, nobody speaks.
An electric, silent fleet for the permitted routes. In winter, along the power-line track; in summer, along the shore.
expeditions.safety: Polar bears are part of this environment. Every outing is accompanied by armed guides with specialist training and deterrent equipment. Always follow their instructions and do not leave the hotel grounds on your own.
expeditions.suspended: No expeditions operate during the temporary closure.

gallery.title:
Chosen objects
to accompany you.
gallery.intro: On the main floor, between the lobby and the restaurant.
shops: Mechanical watches from Swiss and German manufactures, and a small workshop for adjustments and straps.
Pieces by Nordic jewellers, many of them one of a kind.
Technical clothing for being outside at thirty below without giving up looking like yourself.
gallery.photoIntro: The Arca in its first summer.

arrival.title:
Getting
to the Arca.
arrival.intro: First to Longyearbyen. From there, the last stretch by air or by sea: there is no road.
steps: Daily flights from Oslo and several a week from Tromsø.
Forty minutes along the coast to the helipad on our dock. We collect you at the airport.
In summer, about three hours along the coast to our dock. You will see seals and, with luck, whales.
arrival.note: There are no transfers while the temporary closure lasts. Please do not travel to Svalbard to stay at the Arca until we confirm that we have reopened.

team.title:
The people
behind the Arca.
team.intro: Four people responsible for the same promise: care in every detail of your stay.
people: “If something works, it is because someone has checked it three times.”
“If you don’t see me, everything is fine.”
“Up here, small things have to be treated early.”
“What we sell is time. And here, time stands still.”

legal.title: Legal notice
sections: Legal notice

ARCA-∅ is a fictional place from the novel “Arca-∅” by A. Riven. This website is part of its narrative universe. The facilities, team, press quotation, medical services and closure notice are fictional. There is no real accommodation offer and no contracts can be entered into through this website.
Terms of use

The content serves a cultural and promotional purpose for the novel. Images are generated recreations made for this project, not photographs of a real hotel. Travel information is contextual and must not be used to plan expeditions. The work’s texts and identity belong to their respective rights holders.
Privacy

This website has no submission forms, accounts, payments or analytics. Language selection lasts only for the visit and is not saved in your browser. Images and fonts are served from the site’s hosting. GitHub Pages may process technical connection data, including IP addresses, under its own privacy policy. The sound experience stores only the last chapter selected in this browser. The Spotify player loads only when you press its button; your browser then connects to Spotify, which may use its own cookies and process data under its privacy policy.
Email contact

Email links open your email application. Only if you send a message will your provider and the recipient process the included data. Do not send medical or financial information or identity documents. The displayed email may be a configuration placeholder, not an operational service.
Cookies

This site uses no first-party cookies or local storage for tracking. The sound experience remembers the last chapter locally. If you choose to load the external player, Spotify may use cookies from its service. You can listen using the “Open in Spotify” link without loading the player here.
